display.purpose: Hero name/role line and section/case-study headings, in Libre Caslon Display.

body.purpose: Running prose, in IBM Plex Sans.

label.purpose: Field labels, kickers, table headers, stamp brackets, in IBM Plex Mono.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The stamp badge's arrival settle — the system's one authored motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Ink-filled square button, mono label, level with the secondary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 3rem; padding-inline: 1.5rem; border: 1px solid #17181a; background: #17181a; color: #edeae2; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #3f4044; border-color: #3f4044; } .ds-btn-primary:active { translate: 0 1px; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d6291a; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Transparent outlined button, same height and type as the primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 3rem; padding-inline: 1.5rem; border: 1px solid #17181a; background: transparent; color: #17181a; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgb(23 24 26 / 0.05); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { translate: 0 1px; }

components.name: Stamp Badge — Shipped
components.description: Bracketed state mark for a shipped project row.
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; column-gap: 0.5em; } .ds-stamp__bracket { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #5e5f63; } .ds-stamp__label { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #b81f12; }

components.name: Stamp Badge — In Progress
components.description: Quieter, italic bracketed mark for unfinished work — intentionally lower-contrast than Shipped.
components.html: [In progress]

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Transparent, square-cornered field; darkens border on focus, reddens on error.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; min-height: 3rem; padding: 0.375rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid #5e5f63; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: #17181a; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: #17181a; outline: none; } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: #b81f12; }

components.name: Section Navigation Link
components.description: Mono nav link; underlines in Correction Ink on hover/focus, no color change on the text.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: #17181a; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { text-decoration: underline 2px #d6291a; text-underline-offset: 0.3em; }

narrative.overview: This system reads as a printing-house press-proof: a sheet where every claim is checked against a physical mark before it's allowed to stand. Bone paper and near-black proof ink carry the whole page; one saturated red is reserved entirely for the moment something is being verified, corrected, or acted on. Nothing on the page is decorative for its own sake — the registration crosses close every section, the trim marks frame every reproduced screenshot, the ledger tables carry the site's actual claims with dates and commands. The system was chosen by a resonance-ordered concept roll (form: The Proof Sheet, seed key bb5ba904) and built code-led, with no comp; a plain "fd." wordmark with a red dot was kept for the masthead after three cross-based logomark alternatives were explicitly tried and rejected — the system favors restraint over a cleverer, less legible mark.
keyCharacteristics: Flat ink-on-paper at rest; the only depth device is a hairline rule or a trim-mark frame, never a shadow.
Sharp corners everywhere (border-radius: 0) — buttons, inputs, and image frames all meet at right angles.
One accent color, reserved for state and correction, never used as general decoration.
A strict baseline grid (--grid: 0.375rem); line-heights snap up to it via CSS round().
Theme and section-to-section navigation change state instantly — no eased color or layout transition.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Correction Ink appears only where something is being verified, corrected, marked with a state, or focused/hovered — never as a background fill, a decorative rule, or a headline color.

rules.name: The Labeled-Size Rule
rules.body: A specimen heading prints its own live-measured point size in the margin, read off the rendered font-size at runtime rather than hand-typed — the label can never drift out of sync with the type.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth reads through rules and trim marks, never a cast shadow — a shadow would break the flat "printed sheet" premise the whole system stands on.

dos: Do keep Correction Ink to state, correction, and focus/hover moments — never a background fill or a headline color (The One Accent Rule).
Do use square corners everywhere; a rounded corner anywhere in this system reads as a foreign component.
Do use a rule or a trim-mark frame for depth; never a box-shadow (The No-Shadow Rule).
Do cut state changes (theme, active nav) instantly; an eased color transition contradicts the "instant proof mark" premise.
Do reuse the ledger table (claim / how checked / state) for any future page that needs to back a claim with evidence, rather than inventing a new proof device.
donts: Don't draw a tilted double-rule "rubber stamp" shape around a state word — this was tried and rejected; state is marked with plain brackets only.
Don't add a cross-monogram or any icon-based logomark to the masthead — three alternatives were tried and rejected in favor of the plain "fd." + dot mark.
Don't introduce a second accent color; the system's whole restraint argument rests on there being exactly one.
Don't use prefers-reduced-motion as an excuse to drop a state entirely — the stamp badge still animates under reduced motion, just as a plain fade instead of a translate+fade.
